workflow.title: Review old project dependencies before cleaning your Mac
workflow.primaryIntent: Decide whether a 90-day-unused dependency folder is actually rebuildable before scheduling cleanup.
workflow.uniqueMechanism: MacWashing explicitly groups node_modules, Pods and .venv by project age. Use this documented heuristic to explain review, exclusions, environment/lockfile preservation and rebuild cost, not to claim old folders are disposable.
outline: Start with a keep/review/exclude decision, not a savings claim
Explain MacWashing's documented age-based rule and its untested limits
Distinguish dependencies from source, local edits and irreplaceable project data
Review removal mode and exclude active/work folders before considering Auto-Clean
Compare one-off folder review with Breathing Room source-supported owner/project views and sampled activity
Choose the workflow and disclose preview, runtime, hosted-data and paid-service boundaries
workflow.interactionPass: Handoff a non-destructive decision checklist: active project? reproducible environment/lockfiles? local changes? backup? acceptable rebuild/download cost? Unknown answers lead to Keep/Exclude. No shell deletion commands, pretend scanner or automatic folder-safety verdict.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs MacWashing: cleanup rules or activity context?
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between documented rules-based Mac maintenance and a source-available maintenance/activity preview.
comparison.answer: MacWashing is relevant for its documented uninstaller, permission review and scheduled rules-based cleanup. Breathing Room is relevant for its source-supported storage/app/activity investigation, if a non-notarized preview and Python prerequisite are acceptable. Do not equate either with performance improvements or risk-free deletion.

comparison.disclosure: We build Breathing Room; no competitor app was installed or tested.
